questions.prompt: A spread keeps 80% of its gap from the mean each day. What is its half-life?
questions.explanation: The gap after h days is 0.8^h of the start, and half-life solves 0.8^h = 0.5. So h = ln(0.5) / ln(0.8) = -0.6931 / -0.2231 = 3.1 days.

questions.prompt: You fit a line through (yesterday's spread, today's change) and get a slope of +0.01. What should you do with this pair?
options: Trade it with a half-life of 100 days
Drop it: k is above 1, so there is no pull back to the mean
Use a rolling window of 1 day
questions.explanation: The slope is k - 1, so k = 1.01. A gap that keeps more than 100% of itself each day grows instead of closing, and the formula gives no half-life.

questions.prompt: The pair was built with a true half-life of 6.58 days, but the estimate from 500 days of data is 8.1 days. Why?
options: The formula ln(0.5) / ln(k) is only an approximation
The daily random news moves the fitted slope, so the estimate is rough
The hedge ratio was wrong, so the spread is not stationary
questions.explanation: The slope is fitted on noisy daily changes. Even 500 days leave an error of a couple of days here, so treat a half-life as a rough guide.
